segments.content:
Rekindling the Verdant Years Chapter 108: Venturing into a Boy's Territory

About twenty minutes after Xu Youyu called Yan Zhusheng, the doorbell rang.

Xu Youyu, who had nothing left to do in the kitchen, took off her apron, jogged to the entrance, and opened the door for Yan Zhusheng.

The two girls got together, chatting about who knows what on the living room sofa.

Their idle chat was only interrupted when Li Luo called them in to bring out the dishes.

"Have you finished your homework?"

During the meal, Yan Zhusheng looked up at Li Luo across from her and asked.

"Yeah, I'm done."

They had exams from Wednesday to Friday.

With his memory palace, Li Luo had nothing to review.

And the teachers usually assigned the weekend homework in advance after each subject's exam was over.

So, during the study hall periods outside of exam time, Li Luo had already finished all of his assignments.

Although Yan Zhusheng hadn't finished at first, she had also gotten it all done over the past two days at home.

So she said, "The club president asked me to ask you, if you're done with your homework, if you can come practice with us during evening self-study."

"The rock club?" Xu Youyu asked curiously.

Yan Zhusheng nodded, looking at Li Luo with a bit of anticipation in her eyes.

"Sure," Li Luo agreed with a nod. "But can we go during evening self-study? Isn't that outside of the club activity time?"

"The president went to ask the teacher for permission," Yan Zhusheng said. "After all, we have to perform at the parent-teacher conference and the sports meet. It's normal to get a little extra time for training and practice."

"That's true," Xu Youyu nodded, then frowned as she realized something. "Oh right, for the rock club's performance, only the first-year parents will see it. What a shame."

"The second-year parents can't watch?" Li Luo looked puzzled.

"Nope," Xu Youyu said, shaking her head. "The parents of second and third-years already toured the school when we were in the first year. The next two years are just straightforward parent-teacher conferences. They leave right after."

"The campus tours and club showcases are generally planned specifically for first-year parents."

"Otherwise, it would be hard to manage with too many people. It's mainly to show off the school's flair to the first-year parents."

"However…" Xu Youyu's eyes darted around. "I can have my mom sneak in and enjoy you two's performance."

"Your mom is coming to the conference? What about your dad?" Li Luo asked curiously.

"My dad's pretty busy," Xu Youyu waved her hand. "He has to teach and supervise students on weekdays, and he has all sorts of meetings on weekends. My mom has more free time."

"Oh, right," speaking of which, Xu Youyu remembered something and said to Li Luo, "My mom said that after the parent-teacher conference ends, she wants to invite you and Xixi's parents out for a meal."

"After all, we all live together. My mom wants to get to know Uncle and Auntie and become closer so that we can look out for each other if anything comes up."

"About that..." Li Luo stroked his chin. "Xixi's dad isn't free on Saturday, so he can't make it to the conference. I guess only my parents will be able to come then."

"Eh?" Xu Youyu was a little disappointed, then looked at Yan Zhusheng. "What about you, Zhusheng? Maybe you and your family could come along too?"

Yan Zhusheng also shook her head. "Probably not. My mom might not have time."

"Let's see how it goes. No rush," Li Luo said. "If it really doesn't work out, it's fine for just us to have a meal."

After dinner, there was still a lot of time before evening self-study at school.

So Li Luo returned to his bedroom to continue writing.

Xu Youyu and Yan Zhusheng went into the kitchen to wash the dishes.

After washing up, Xu Youyu returned to her bedroom, turned on her computer to take a look, and was pleasantly surprised to find that someone had gifted her a Lord-level donation.

She looked closely. The ID was "Chongran."

Well then… so it was that guy Li Luo.

The corners of Xu Youyu's mouth curled up. She thought to herself that the boy had some manners after all, knowing to return a favor.

However, when she habitually opened her comment section, she saw that Li Luo, under the alias "Chongran," had left a comment in her review section.

And it was a long one at that.

Chongran: This book, "The Literary Era," is my favorite entertainment-themed work of the year, bar none.

Then, Li Luo elaborated in detail why he thought the book was well-written, starting from the content, writing style, plot tone, pacing, and even some very minor points.

Xu Youyu's eyes sparkled as she read, her heart leaping uncontrollably from Li Luo's praise. This kind of well-reasoned praise was far more gratifying than simple, awkward flattery.

It gave her a pleasant feeling, like her soul was at a spa.

One section about acting, in particular, not only made Xu Youyu feel a sense of shared experience but also a comfort and emotion of having met a kindred spirit, of being deeply understood by Li Luo.

Chongran: I write in the entertainment genre myself, but if I want to describe a character's good acting, I usually only have two methods.

Chongran: One is through indirect description, by depicting the onlookers' emotions changing from initial disdain to later amazement and admiration, to indirectly highlight the brilliance of the character's acting.

Chongran: The other is also an indirect description of the character, again not writing about the acting itself, but focusing on the efforts the character made for the role, such as an actress cutting off her long hair, or an overweight actor losing dozens of pounds in a month, things like that.

Chongran: But this book, "The Literary Era," is different. While it masterfully employs the two techniques above, it also dares to directly describe something as abstract and mysterious as acting.

Chongran: It's like solving a problem. Using a method similar to film analysis, it lists the performance requirements for a scene, and then directly describes the details of the actor's body language that, with a snap, sketch out that feeling.

Chongran: This direct approach of using words to convey "superb acting" is something 99% of entertainment genre authors can't do.

On this point alone, Li Luo had written a lengthy discourse of several hundred words. The entire long review, if counted, was probably thousands of words long.

Xu Youyu subconsciously bit her lip lightly.

People who don't write books might not understand.

Often, even a reader's simple comment like "it's great" can keep an author happy for a long time.

And a long, highly positive review like this, with well-reasoned, point-by-point praise, would give an author the surprise of meeting a kindred spirit.

It felt like her entire heart was trembling, and her whole body was tingling.

"He's pretty good at giving praise… this guy." Xu Youyu propped her feet on her chair, hugged her knees, and carefully reread the long review several more times.

She smiled every time she read it. It started as a smile with pursed lips, but eventually, the smile spread across her entire face, a change Xu Youyu herself didn't even notice.

SleepEarlyGrowTaller: My Lord-level donation was not in vain. I've pinned your review!

At a little past six in the evening, Yan Zhusheng, who was relaxing by playing the piano in the piano room, glanced at the time.

She then stood up, walked out of the piano room, and came to the door of Xu Youyu's bedroom.

But after a moment's thought, she didn't knock. Instead, she continued down the hallway, all the way to Li Luo's bedroom door.

Knock, knock, knock.

"Come in."

Hearing Li Luo's voice, Yan Zhusheng pushed the door open and poked her head in, looking around curiously.

This was her first time inside a boy's bedroom.

As if exploring an unknown world, Yan Zhusheng walked in cautiously and looked at Li Luo at his desk.

Perhaps because he already knew that she was aware he was a writer, Li Luo wasn't on guard against her. He was still clacking away on the keyboard and said without turning his head, "Almost done. Have a seat for a moment."

"Oh," Yan Zhusheng blinked, glanced around, but couldn't find a chair to sit on. So she had to walk to the bed and sit on its edge beside the desk.

As the soft mattress supported her hips, Yan Zhusheng propped her right hand on the bed, a strange feeling rising in her heart.

"Ahem, ahem… don't look," Li Luo noticed Yan Zhusheng peeking at his screen. He immediately raised a hand to block it and said, a little embarrassed, "I can't write when someone's watching."

It was like using the bathroom. If someone was staring at you the whole time, something would just feel off, and you couldn't put any force into it.

"Oh…" Yan Zhusheng obediently averted her gaze, placed her hands properly back on her knees, and waited quietly. Her eyes, however, darted all around, wanting to get a better look at Li Luo's bedroom.

(End of this chapter)
